title: Questions on the Lock Reserve in Gift Cards & Store Credit Cash-Outs
content:
**What is the lock reserve?** After a lock on a Gift Cards & Store Credit instrument has been lifted, a lock reserve is kept back from the instrument's current balance less the held refunded value (the refunded value still held while the refund availability period runs). The lock reserve is rounded half up to the cent, stays on the instrument and is taken off the cash-out amount.

**How large is it?** It depends on when the instrument's most recent lock was placed, counted in calendar days before the cash-out date, as shown by the lock date on the instrument's record:

| Most recent lock placed | Lock reserve |
|---|---|
| At most 30 calendar days before the cash-out date | 0.25 of the current balance less the held refunded value |
| More than 30 but at most 90 calendar days before | 0.10 of that amount |
| Earlier than 90 calendar days before, or the instrument was never locked | No lock reserve |

**Where are the edges?** (hypothetical lock dates)

| Days between the most recent lock and the cash-out date | Reserve share |
|---|---|
| 0 (locked and unlocked on the cash-out date itself) | 0.25 |
| 30 | 0.25 |
| 31 | 0.10 |
| 90 | 0.10 |
| 91 | none |

**What does it come to on figures?** (hypothetical instruments)

- Current balance 8.00, no refunded value held, most recent lock 20 days ago: 8.00 multiplied by 0.25 gives a reserve of 2.00.
- Current balance 8.00, held refunded value 3.00, most recent lock 45 days ago: 5.00 multiplied by 0.10 gives a reserve of 0.50.
- Current balance 7.30, nothing held, most recent lock 10 days ago: 7.30 multiplied by 0.25 is 1.825, rounded half up to 1.83.
